```{r, results='asis'}
# Custom function to truncate author list (keep first 3 + last 3)
truncate_authors <- function(authors) {
  if (is.null(authors) || length(authors) == 0) return("Unknown")
  # Handle person objects from bibtex
  if (inherits(authors, "person")) {
    author_list <- format(authors, include = c("given", "family"))
  } else {
    authors <- as.character(authors)
    author_list <- trimws(strsplit(authors, " and ")[[1]])
  }
  n <- length(author_list)
  if (n > 7) {
    # Show first 3, ..., last 3
    first_three <- paste(author_list[1:3], collapse = ", ")
    last_three <- paste(author_list[(n-2):n], collapse = ", ")
    paste0(first_three, ", ..., ", last_three)
  } else {
    paste(author_list, collapse = ", ")
  }
}

bib <- bibtex::read.bib(bibfile) %>%
  purrr::keep(~ attr(.x, "bibtype") %in% c("Article", "Online"))

# Sort by year descending
years <- purrr::map_chr(bib, ~ as.character(as.numeric(.x$year) %||% "0"))
bib <- bib[order(years, decreasing = TRUE)]

# Use existing BibTeX keywords as initial subject tags. Both comma- and
# semicolon-separated keyword fields are supported.
publication_tags <- function(entry) {
  keywords <- as.character(entry$keywords %||% "")
  keywords <- unlist(strsplit(keywords, "[,;]"))
  # Collapse internal whitespace/newlines from multi-line BibTeX fields
  keywords <- trimws(gsub("\\s+", " ", gsub("[{}]", "", keywords)))
  keywords <- keywords[nzchar(keywords)]
  if (length(keywords) == 0) {
    keywords <- "General public health"
  }
  unique(keywords)
}

slugify <- function(value) {
  value <- tolower(gsub("[^[:alnum:]]+", "-", value))
  gsub("(^-|-$)", "", value)
}

all_tags <- sort(unique(unlist(purrr::map(bib, publication_tags))))
all_tag_slugs <- purrr::map_chr(all_tags, slugify)
# Guard against distinct tags slugifying to the same id (e.g. differing only
# by punctuation/whitespace), which would otherwise collide as object keys.
all_tags <- all_tags[!duplicated(all_tag_slugs)]
all_tag_slugs <- all_tag_slugs[!duplicated(all_tag_slugs)]

# Render filter options after the BibTeX file has been parsed so the controls
# always stay in sync with the available publication tags.
cat(
  '<script>window.publicationTags = ',
  jsonlite::toJSON(stats::setNames(as.list(all_tags), all_tag_slugs), auto_unbox = TRUE),
  ';</script>\n',
  '<script src="publication-filter.js" defer></script>\n'
)

# Render each publication
purrr::walk(bib, function(entry) {
  authors <- truncate_authors(entry$author)
  title <- as.character(entry$title %||% "Untitled")
  title <- gsub("[{}]", "", title)
  journal <- as.character(entry$journal %||% "")
  journal <- gsub("[{}]", "", journal)
  year <- as.character(entry$year %||% "")
  doi <- as.character(entry$doi %||% "")
  tags <- publication_tags(entry)
  tag_ids <- paste(purrr::map_chr(tags, slugify), collapse = " ")
  tags_html <- paste(
    purrr::map_chr(tags, function(tag) {
      sprintf('<span class="pub-tag">%s</span>', htmlEscape(tag))
    }),
    collapse = " "
  )

  if (doi != "" && !is.na(doi)) {
    title_html <- sprintf('<a href="https://doi.org/%s">%s</a>', doi, title)
  } else {
    title_html <- title
  }

  cat(sprintf(
    '<div class="pub-item" data-tags="%s"><strong>%s</strong> (%s). %s. <em>%s</em>.<div class="pub-tags">%s</div></div>\n',
    htmlEscape(tag_ids), authors, year, title_html, journal, tags_html
  ))
})
```
